name: Glenn Ivey

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: IN THE MATTER OF ALLEGATIONS RELATING TO REPRESENTATIVE CHUCK EDWARDS
statements.title: IN THE MATTER OF ALLEGATIONS RELATING TO REPRESENTATIVE CHUCK EDWARDS
sentences: As the report details on page 4 of the report: ``Both women received numerous gifts from Representative Edwards, including jewelry totaling over $1,000, designer purses, guns, shoes, flowers, a laptop and cell phone, KitchenAid mixer, robotic vacuum, vacations, tickets to performances, and one-on-one dinners.'' The tickets to performances, that wasn't just any performance.
This isn't congratulations on your wedding or that new baby that was born.
There are going to come times when we need to go outside of the House of Representatives and refer these cases to law enforcement because some of the sexual misconduct isn't just sexual harassment.
Mr. Speaker, the last point I will make on this, and this is in the wake of some of the other--not investigations before the committee right now, but some of the other things we have heard.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: CONGRESSIONAL BLACK CAUCUS HIT THE GROUND RUNNING IN AUGUST
statements.title: CONGRESSIONAL BLACK CAUCUS HIT THE GROUND RUNNING IN AUGUST
sentences: Other people who have to drive for a living, people who drive trucks, the cost of diesel, for example--I don't have many farmers in my district, but for them, diesel is up $2 a gallon.
Schoolbuses are back for schools in most places across the country, and most of those run on diesel fuel.
I mentioned that a minute ago, but I want to come back to that because the tariffs have been awful in the impact that they have had on grocery prices.
That is because the tariffs have caused grocery prices and other prices across the board to go up for no reason.

One of my colleagues mentioned earlier that the Trump administration and many of my Republican colleagues are telling you it is not the consumers that are paying these tariffs; it is the foreign countries that the goods come from.
Remember a couple of months ago when the Supreme Court said that the Trump tariffs were illegal and had to be refunded?
For consumers, who also paid these tariffs, taxes, and higher prices, there is nothing out there for them to get the money back that they paid that the Supreme Court said was illegal.

It is just about helping the bigger businesses, the ones that are already the billionaires, the ones that are already making lots of money, the ones that make huge contributions to the Trump administration and the families--huge contributions, I mean billions of dollars in cryptocurrency and the like.
I have to mention some, but I will go back to some other topics, other aspects of that, as well.
I won't get into the accountability piece.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: GUN VIOLENCE AWARENESS MONTH
statements.title: GUN VIOLENCE AWARENESS MONTH
sentences: I came up and didn't really know much about gun violence until I became a prosecutor, first here in Washington, D.C., at the U.S. Attorney's Office.
A mother and a father were having trouble with their son, and they called because it was a mental health call.
We had an assault weapons ban in the United States in the nineties.
I looked around and thought if we can't do assault weapon bans, what about ghost guns?
Ghost guns came out maybe not even 10 years ago.
For those of you that don't know, ghost guns are guns that do not have serial numbers on them.
Between 2017 and 2023, there was a 1,600 percent jump in the use of ghost guns at crime scenes.
Democrats offered two bills to ban ghost guns and do it in different ways.
Hundreds of Democrats signed on, not one Republican signed on to either bill, either piece of legislation to ban ghost guns.
The use of ghost guns in crimes continued to go up.

The Biden administration said to the ATF, issue a regulation, base it on the Gun Control Act, which is the longstanding law that covers gun usage and the regulation of guns in the United States, and maybe that will help.
It is an infringement on our constitutional rights, our Second Amendment rights.
It was taken to court and worked its way up to the Supreme Court.
Guess what happened at the Supreme Court: 7-2 margin in Bondi v. Vanderstok.
The Supreme Court said: We are going to uphold this regulation.
In fact, all three Trump Supreme Court appointees joined in the majority of that opinion.
We know that only criminals want to use ghost guns.
It is certainly useful for law enforcement.
It can't be on those grounds, and it can't be constitutional grounds because the Trump Supreme Court by 7-2 vote just told them this does not violate the Second Amendment.
It is not just the ghost guns piece.
As you just heard a few minutes ago, many of the programs that are aimed at reducing gun violence, including for suicides, have been cut by the Trump administration.

Matter fact, one of the first things the Trump administration did when they came into office was to eliminate grants that helped reduce gun violence across the country that had been proven to work over the past few years.
The Trump administration also cut funding to address gun violence prevention, $66 million for assistance for gun violence victims, $82 million for law enforcement support and training and safety.
I think that the goal, at least that I came here with, was to try and find ways to address gun violence.
I thought ghost gun restrictions would be one way to go.

We put out a bill called Raise the Age, and the thinking on that was, if we raise the age from 18 to 21 for people purchasing assault weapons, they will be okay with that because it moved from 18 to 21 when Reagan was President.
If we are going to have 21 for handguns, shouldn't we also have it for assault weapons?

I know there is a lot of political challenges here and, frankly, we will keep working at it, but I knew when Republican colleagues were shot and Democratic colleagues have been shot, when we have been victimized by gun violence and we still can't move on legislation to address gun violence, then I don't know that there is enough to make it happen.

I think we have to continue to keep fighting and keep working to address this problem because the homicides keep happening, the bodies keep falling, the chalk lines around them keep being drawn, and the pools of blood oozing out of their bodies until the police get there to try to fix the problem that, in many instances, these guns are too powerful to allow them to be fixed.
I certainly don't agree with a lot that has been done by my Republican colleagues--surely, in the cuts and especially to the ghost gun regulation.

I can't figure out why we would want to restrict information from being gathered so that researchers and scientists can try to figure out other approaches to reduce gun violence, other than just enforcement.
Why shouldn't we study them to see if we can expand them to see if we can find ways to combine enforcement with intervention and prevention efforts and reverse gun violence even more?
I can't say I am super-hopeful right now, but I truly believe that we can find a way to protect people's Second Amendment rights and also protect second graders.
We also have to find ways to protect law enforcement officers, who put their lives on the line out there on the street and are particularly at risk from gun violence, as well.

statements.title: SELF-ENRICHMENT REWARDED, OVERSIGHT BLINDFOLDED

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: NATIONAL POLICE WEEK
statements.title: NATIONAL POLICE WEEK
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I rise today in observance of National Police Week.

One of those names was my cousin, Earl Ivey, Jr. He served as an officer for the Mount Rainier Police Department, the Office of the Sheriff, the Seat Pleasant Police Department, and he did double duty as chief and chaplain of the Fairmount Heights Police Department.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: FOURTH ANNIVERSARY OF THE TOPS SUPERMARKET SHOOTING IN BUFFALO, NEW YORK
statements.title: FOURTH ANNIVERSARY OF THE TOPS SUPERMARKET SHOOTING IN BUFFALO, NEW YORK
sentences: I thank the Gun Violence Prevention Task Force and the Congressional Black Caucus for joining in as well in support of this effort.
As you just heard from my colleague, 10 people were gunned down using an assault weapon that had been sold to an 18-year-old, an AR-15 that had been modified.
Schools now sell bulletproof backpacks to protect kids--``protect kids''--from this kind of gun violence and bulletproof chalkboards.
We have talked a little bit about some of the solutions to gun violence.
The ghost gun piece, in particular, was a shock for me.
Ghost guns, as you may know, are untraceable guns.
The only reason somebody would want a gun that is untraceable is if you want to commit a crime and you want to make sure that law enforcement cannot find you.
The Trump Supreme Court, to my surprise, upheld that regulation.
Yesterday, in the Committee on Appropriations, I am sorry to say, my Republican colleagues passed language that would repeal the ban on ghost guns.
You heard about the assault weapons ban.
I put together a bill that is called Raise the Age, and it would raise the age from 18 to 21 to buy an assault-style weapon.
It is already required that you be 21 to buy handguns, and that was a bill that was put in place by the Ronald Reagan administration.
The shooter in Charleston, he was 21, but he should have been caught by the background check.
The funds that would be used to help prevent street violence or, even worse, gun violence in our schools has been cut back.
My Republican colleagues want to protect the Second Amendment.
That is great, but we have got to be able to find a way to protect the Second Amendment and protect second-graders at the same time.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: ANOTHER BLIGHT ON AMERICAN HISTORY
statements.title: ANOTHER BLIGHT ON AMERICAN HISTORY
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I thank my colleague from Virginia for leading this Special Order tonight and my colleagues who have spoken on the floor in shock and dismay with respect to what the Supreme Court did in the Voting Rights Act ruling just a few days ago, and also what the Virginia Supreme Court did in the ruling that it passed down.
I reminded them that Dr. Martin Luther King was only 25 when he led the Montgomery bus boycott and was still working on his dissertation and raising a family, all at the same time.

I reminded them that the Freedom Riders had people on at 18, 19, and 20 years old who they forced to write and sign wills before they got on those buses because they knew that they would be violently attacked, and they were.

We have to make sure we get out there and do that work, push in the streets, campaign, stand up, make sure we fight, speak, have our voices heard, and bring everybody out who we can because it is critical for us to win in November in order to turn this around and show them that, despite all the efforts that they have made--the Trump Supreme Court, the seizure of the ballots, all the things that they have been doing with the executive orders and the like--we can defeat all of those in November.
But we have to show up, and we will.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: JANUARY 6 ATTACK
statements.title: JANUARY 6 ATTACK
sentences: He was a police officer who had grown up in Prince George's County.
He had mixed feelings about what the police do because he had had some bad experiences in his childhood and in his neighborhood, but he decided he could make a difference.
He felt called to public service as a police officer.

When he went to work, he joined the Metropolitan Police Department in Washington, D.C., and was sent to some of the toughest neighborhoods in Washington, where I had actually been a prosecutor many years before.

Mr. Tate, formerly Officer Tate, felt so betrayed by what had happened--not just that day, not just by the way some Members of Congress have responded to what happened that day, and not just by the pardon--that he actually left the police department.
He didn't feel he could be a police officer again.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: MEDICAL BILLS ARE TOO HIGH
statements.title: MEDICAL BILLS ARE TOO HIGH
sentences: Not only did they not address extending the tax credits for the Affordable Care Act, but they made the problem even worse.
The big, ugly bill that they passed included a $1 trillion cut to Medicaid.
I know my Republican colleagues have been fighting against ObamaCare for years now.
There were over 60 votes to repeal and replace the ObamaCare piece of legislation.
Somewhere along the way, about 5 years in, they found out that the American people actually like ObamaCare.

They might call it the Affordable Care Act, but they kind of liked not having pregnancy treated as a preexisting condition, and they kind of liked having the ability to have their kids stay on their family insurance plans until they turned 26.
Monthly payments for him and his wife will rise from $670 to $2,054.
They came into office on January 20th knowing that these ACA tax credits were going to expire.
I will help you out with it, but when is it due?

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: DISTRICT OF COLUMBIA CASH BAIL REFORM ACT OF 2025
statements.title: DISTRICT OF COLUMBIA CASH BAIL REFORM ACT OF 2025
sentences: In addition to that, roughly 40 States in the Union are patterned after the Federal Bail Reform Act, just like the D.C. bill is, but there is no effort to change those.

Under Salerno, the Supreme Court case which ruled on the constitutionality of this language over 40 years ago, the Supreme Court said that there are a variety of safeguards that have been put in place: right to counsel, detention hearing, and the chance to offer opposing evidence and the like, that provides the safeguards that permit the statute to be found to be constitutional.
Mr. Speaker, I rise in opposition to this legislation.
Mr. Speaker, I would say at this point, though, that because it is unconstitutional, I urge my Republican colleagues to oppose this bill.
I urge all of my colleagues to oppose this bill.
I oppose it even if you do the revision piece, Mr. Speaker, because I think it violates the rights of the District of Columbia to make their own determinations.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: DISTRICT OF COLUMBIA POLICING PROTECTION ACT
statements.title: DISTRICT OF COLUMBIA POLICING PROTECTION ACT
sentences: I know he has a strong respect for law enforcement, so I am not saying his heart is in the wrong place, but I am saying this bill is wrong.

He is right, I was never in an active car pursuit, but I was a prosecutor here in Washington, D.C., and for 8 years in Prince George's County, which is the eastern border of Washington, D.C., so I have seen the results of some of these high-speed chases.
A police officer saw a stolen motorcycle zip down the beltway and decided to pursue it.
Mind you, this is during rush hour, so he had to pursue on the border of the road, and speeds got up to over 100 miles an hour on the beltway in rush hour.
The Washington Post just did a piece about the Park Police.
Mr. Speaker, I thank my colleague for yielding, and I rise in strong opposition to the gentleman's bill.
We had several, but I will just pick one for purposes of time.
The last point I will make, a variation on the home rule argument.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: DEVASTATING HARM CAUSED BY TRUMP ADMINISTRATION
statements.title: DEVASTATING HARM CAUSED BY TRUMP ADMINISTRATION
sentences: It looked kind of like a state of the Union, but it wasn't actually that address, but there was a young boy up in the seats over there who was a cancer survivor.

They can't develop them fast enough, and they are pushing them into research and work with respect to artificial intelligence and quantum computing, while here in the United States, especially in the last 9 months, we are doing everything we can--well, the Trump administration is doing everything it can, it would seem, to limit the number of people who can go into this kind of work.
Mr. Speaker, 445,000 Federal employees lost their collective bargaining rights.
Some of the attacks on Harvard, in particular, the big threat was: We are not going to let you have international students come to study.
That is the only way we are going to be able to win the competition with China.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: WEAPONIZATION OF ICE
statements.title: WEAPONIZATION OF ICE
sentences: Just this weekend, I had a chance to see Trump Border Czar Tom Homan talking about how the administration is conducting the sweeps on the streets and that they are doing it to prioritize public safety and national security.
The conservative Cato Institute found that only 7 percent of detainees were violent criminals.
In fact, most detainees aren't even criminals at all.
For example, some people were waiting at bus stops and having coffee when they were then surrounded by ICE agents in unmarked vehicles that sped up in their direction.
The court who was reviewing these cases questioned what it was about the bus stop that caused these ICE agents to believe they had reasonable suspicion to detain these men.

The court reviewed it and found that the government said: It was based on their past experiences that have demonstrated that illegal aliens utilize and seek to work at certain places, like getting their car washed or waiting for the bus.

Like the unlawful deportation of Kilmar Abrego Garcia and the willful defiance of a unanimous Supreme Court decision to bring him back, the Trump administration is unapologetic in its efforts to target immigrants, the Constitution, and the law be damned.

Now, in addition to being unconstitutional, this wastes a great deal of tax dollars because they are detaining masses of people in these large sweeps, only to have to release them when proof of their legal status is shown.
Remember the so-called Venezuelan violent gang members deported to the gulag in El Salvador.
They were in the United States legally, and they hadn't committed any kind of crimes in El Salvador or Venezuela.
This is not the best use of our Federal law enforcement agents.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF SENATE AMENDMENT TO H.R. 1, ONE BIG BEAUTIFUL BILL ACT
statements.title: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF SENATE AMENDMENT TO H.R. 1, ONE BIG BEAUTIFUL BILL ACT
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I ask unanimous consent to amend the rule to make in order the amendment at the desk that protects against any cuts to Medicaid and SNAP.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: DIVERSITY, EQUITY, AND INCLUSION: ERASING BLACK HISTORY
statements.title: DIVERSITY, EQUITY, AND INCLUSION: ERASING BLACK HISTORY
sentences: It talked about how great they were as generals, and the fact that if they only had an equal amount of supplies as the Union generals, they would have been able to win the war.
You may recall, back in June 2021, this issue came up where they were challenging him with respect to something that was called critical race theory.
We won't go into all of that, but keep in mind that K-12 schools never taught critical race theory.
That doesn't make me a Communist.'' He then offered an argument for expanding political studies in the service of defending the Constitution after the January 6 attack on the Capitol.

What is it that caused thousands of people to assault this building and try to overturn the Constitution of the United States of America?'' Just a little aside on that point, there is a plaque that has been requested to be posted here in the Capitol that represents the brave men and women of the Capitol Police who fought to protect the people who were trapped here by the attacking mob.
It noted that he was court-martialed, but eventually acquitted, after refusing to move to the back of an Army bus in 1944.
In fact, after World War II, he reenlisted for ground combat in Korea.

It kicked up such a controversy, the White House Press Secretary, Karoline Leavitt, said there were quite concerning things that she had done at the Library of Congress in the pursuit of DEI and putting inappropriate books in the Library for children.
With this decision, Donald Trump continues his attempts to censor our history, bend our culture to his will, and interfere with the free flow of information among the American people.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: BIG, BACKSTABBING BILL
statements.title: BIG, BACKSTABBING BILL
sentences: Trump's economic failures include trying to make his tax cuts permanent, the DOGE cuts, and the irresponsibility of the tariff packages.

When he does things like puts up 130-something percent in tariffs against one of the main trading partners of the United States, like China, it creates a major problem for companies that trade with China and that get their materials or send their finished products to China.
In fact, he just moved forward with the tariffs that he put in place.
With respect to reconciliation, as we just talked about a moment ago, the $881 billion in cuts to Medicaid are a shocking development.
It was talking about a district in a rural area where I think they said that 70 percent of their funding comes through Medicaid in one way or another.
One of our colleagues referenced earlier about how that has had a positive impact on the starvation issues, the USAID efforts.
However, they are cutting programs that will to lead to, I saw one estimate, 1.6 million people who will die over the next year based on these cuts that he is making right now to foreign aid.
He is making cuts to mental health services.

We have got kids who need assistance with their mental health challenges across the country, and making cuts to those sorts of programs only makes it harder for these kids to survive and get through the school process.

However, one of the things we can all agree on for sure is that we know the Russians and the Chinese and, in some instances, Iran and terrorist organizations around the world are making efforts to influence our elections with misinformation, disinformation, and the like.
The $881 billion in cuts to Medicaid is over the line.
I will stop with this regarding the plane.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: TRUMP'S FIRST 100 DAYS
statements.title: TRUMP'S FIRST 100 DAYS
sentences: I had one friend tell me that his 401(k) had turned into a 101(K) after Trump put his destructive tariffs in place.
It has been damaging not just for people who own stocks, not just for people who are small business owners, but for every American across the country.

Now, closures of rural and urban hospitals in many instances are going to be a result of the Medicaid cuts that they are talking about making right now, and that is not just President Trump, that is some of my House Republican colleagues here, too.

These are the type of funds, grants that have been making a difference in law enforcement across the country and in fights against things like domestic violence and sexual abuse, and he is making the cuts there, too.
As a matter of fact, we have seen this administration illegally deny due process rights despite a Supreme Court order to return my constituent, Kilmar Abrego Garcia, back to the United States.
The Supreme Court said: You need to facilitate his return.
Last week, when President Trump did an interview, he said, yeah, he could just pick up the phone and have him brought back, but he is not going to do it, despite the Supreme Court order.
The judges who have told him that are not just the Supreme Court but sometimes conservative Republican judges like Judge Wilkinson in the Fourth Circuit based in Richmond.
Let me talk a little bit about tariffs.
Yet, his tariffs have sent the Nation into a tailspin.
Mr. Speaker, I guess you could say there are times when tariffs might make sense, but he did it the exact worst way possible that it could be done.
He did tariffs on all countries and on all products at the exact same time.
There is no way that can work, and there is no reason to do it because sometimes tariffs are placed on things that we don't even make in the United States.
Why is he imposing tariffs on those items?
Then, the tariffs he imposed on some of our best allies, like Canada, disrupted the automobile market.
He backed off of the giant tariffs that he put in, but he left 10 percent tariffs in place.
At some point, it is going to be zillions, I suppose, with those sorts of tariffs.
I guess that was his best ``bah, humbug'' imitation to sort of make light of the fact that these tariffs that he has put in place are going to make things more expensive for the American people.
President Trump, Elon Musk, and their billionaire buddies have pushed a budget that is nothing short of a war on working families.
While Trump and House Republicans push for new handouts for the wealthy, we have massive cuts to Medicare, Medicaid, Social Security, and SNAP.

This is an administration that rules not with hope but with fear, and it is using the machinery of government not to serve the people but to punish the President's perceived enemies, including those who brought January 6 rioters to justice.
The prosecution of the January 6 rioters resulted in more than 1,000 convictions.
They had all worked on January 6 investigations.
They think maybe it is a good thing to get rid of government workers, but I am asking people to keep in mind the dire consequences of these terminations.
Mr. Speaker, I will stop with this one, just on the government cuts piece.
I will chat a little bit about the rule of law issue here, too.
I will take just a moment on that.
As we move past 100 days, I will never stop fighting for those I represent against the abuses of this administration.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: SUPPORTING FEDERAL WORKERS
statements.title: SUPPORTING FEDERAL WORKERS
sentences: Mr. Speaker, a few hours ago, I stood with members of unions, employees at the Department of Labor, and people walking down the street who saw what we were doing and wanted to join in and support the cause.

Lastly, I thank all of those people out there, whether they are union members or attorneys or employees, who are fighting every day to get their point across and make sure that we are heard by the Trump administration.
We cannot allow the Trump administration to replace a competitive merit system with a political spoils system.
That is why we will keep fighting in Congress and the courts.
I urge you to continue to do the work that you are doing because it is making a difference.
